title: Trusted eval artifacts stewardship and access control
creator: Samir Kapoor
description:
Goal: Define and ship a robust stewardship model for 'trusted eval artifacts' (trusted prompt sets, golden examples, and labeled datasets) so that model/config changes can be automatically gated by reproducible evals. Scope includes: access controls for steward roles, immutable artifact identifiers, signed change history, retention and archival policies, and CI/CD gating hooks for model/config rollouts. This ticket drives product requirements and acceptance criteria; ENG will implement storage + signing primitives and a small console UI for stewarding and viewing change history. Out of scope for this ticket: full RBAC integration with SSO (follow-up) and enterprise legal retention variations (policy doc to be created separately).

Background: we have recurrent regression incidents where model or runtime config changes cause quality regressions because prompt bundles changed without a clear audit trail. Existing prompt curation efforts are ad hoc; this work standardizes stewardship so eval runs can be tied to artifact versions and approvals.

Deliverables: product PRD for stewarding flows, UX wireframe for console listing and diff view, evaluation CI gating spec, and a pilot with two internal steward groups (chat-product and search).
acceptance_criteria: Trusted artifacts have immutable content-addressable IDs (CAS URL or content hash) and optional human-friendly alias
Every change to a trusted artifact produces a signed changelog entry with user, timestamp, and rationale
Steward role(s) can create, approve, deprecate, and archive artifacts through a minimal UI or API; audit entries visible in console
CI gating hook can block canary or rollout when a model/config change reduces eval score by more than configurable thresholds using a linked artifact
Migration path for existing golden prompt bundles with mapping guidance and a one-click import script for up to 5k examples
Docs and runbook for incident responders showing how to map regressions to artifact changes and roll back to a previous artifact version

decisions: Use content-addressable storage (sha256 hashes) as canonical artifact ID so references in eval runs are deterministic
Require KMS-backed cryptographic signing for 'approver' actions; signatures stored alongside artifact metadata to provide tamper evidence
Adopt a minimal steward role model initially (creator/editor, approver) rather than complex RBAC; will integrate full SSO groups in a follow-up ticket
Implement CI gating as a configurable threshold policy: absolute delta + relative percent change, evaluated against a canonical eval job that references the artifact hash
Support soft deprecation (artifact remains immutable and referencable) instead of destructive deletes; archive flag and retention policy enforced by lifecycle job
